title: Counter rewind to the destination state
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $q$ and $q'$ be states among the $35$ states, and suppose that in state $q$ the machine, whenever work tape $0$ has a symbol under its head, moves that head one cell left and stays in state $q$, while otherwise it moves the head one cell right and enters state $q'$. For any $i\le |x|$, counter length $n$, and $r\le n$, start in state $q$ with input position just before position $i$, the unary counter of length $n$ with its head at $r-1$, an arbitrary second work tape with head at $b$, and output $o$. After exactly $r+1$ steps the machine is in state $q'$ at the same input position, with the same counter tape and second work tape, counter head at $0$, second head at $b$, and output $o$.
hypotheses_covered: specified transition on occupied versus blank counter cell
arbitrary second tape content and head position $b$
replaced:
Let $q$ be a transducer state whose transition moves the counter head left while
its cell is occupied and otherwise steps right into a destination state. For every
$r \le n$, starting from the canonical frame with counter length $n$ and counter
head at offset $r - 1$, exactly $r + 1$ silent transitions reach the destination
state with the counter head at $0$; input position, buffer, and output are
untouched.
